title: Coordinator: pre-launch scaffolding and workflow render

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text:
Pre-launch complete. Scaffolding committed at 00445c6 (tests/acceptance.sh, bin/delegate-audit, docs/acceptance/build-start.txt). Running acceptance rather than trusting it found two defects in it, both fixed before commit: padded-only item matching (the plan's rows expect 'ACCEPT 3', not 'ACCEPT 03' - would have failed every acceptance row from W0.6 on), and a privacy-scan hit that still printed the offending line to stdout, the stream the final close commits into a public repo. Both lints red-proofed (planted unknown blocked_by -> FAIL unknown-dep; planted unknown alias -> FAIL unknown-alias). Rendered ROUTES match the plan's routing block exactly. Dry run clean: 70 items, 38 tasks, 9 checkpoints, 23 closes, 207 stages, 113 declared-not-run verify rows, every checkpoint gate_required true.

Orchestrator ruling: raised workflows.itemThreads to 96 in the global delegate config. The compiled script's item_thread_cap() reads that file by a hardcoded path and ignores the realm config, so the 70-item plan refused against a 64-item cap that could not be raised where it appeared to live. Runtime config only; no plan, route, or task change. Cost if wrong: a wider admission ceiling than needed, which does not force parallelism. Papercut filed against writing-plans.

Two rulings open with Fable (posted 20260920-030735-674111-68abf8), neither blocking launch: (1) the final-close audit row carries the plan's absolute home path and its output is committed as docs/acceptance/audit-report.md in a public repo - binds before the W2.G close; (2) the --final stage marker spellings, an interface no lane owns - binds before the M2 lanes that emit them.

title: Review v1 spec against the product vision
description: Trey requested Astra's first assessment of the current spec: what serves the vision, what is missing, and what should change, be added, or be removed. Review only; no ratification, implementation, or spec edits.
notes: First review recommends revision before ratification. Product: move context/propose and a minimal census into the first useful slice; run semantic feasibility work before dependent effect/capability promises; make enforcement limits machine-checkable; measure repeated task outcomes and human burden. Acceptance: specify protected gate execution and runner provenance; test the exact materialized candidate; default to fresh integrated evidence rather than import-closure carry-over. Policy: distinguish canonical rules from snapshot-instantiated obligations; compare prospective permissions, not only current obligation sets; anchor approved policy outside candidate discretion. Contradictions: judgment review blocks acceptance despite D3 wording; gate principal arrangement conflicts with trust assumptions; tree IDs do not establish ancestry; draft narrowing ratification is ambiguous. Supporting source sections: 3.7, 6.5, 7.4-7.6, 9.1-9.2, 10.1, 11.1-11.7, 12.3-12.4, 13.3-13.4, 16.4, 17.5, 19.6, 20.2, 21. Findings are specification-level, not tested vulnerabilities. Spec and ratification bead unchanged.

Verification: full spec and vision read, source claims cross-checked against named sections, prose review, git diff --check. No implementation exists to test.

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text:
Coordinator ruling F1 (Fable, 2026-09-20), final-close audit receipt. The compiler bakes an absolute plan path into the close's delegate-audit row and the close commits that output as docs/acceptance/audit-report.md; this repository is public. Ruling: redact at the close step, then scan, then commit - repository root to '.', any home directory to '~', every occurrence and not only the plan path, then the same privacy expressions tests/acceptance.sh uses, refusing the commit on a hit, applied to every receipt the close commits. Implemented in bin/delegate-audit at 55f120b, since the close copies whatever that shim prints. Downside of record: the committed receipt is no longer byte-identical to the tool's stdout, and the M2 review record states that the audit report is redacted by this rule. The durable fix is compiler-side; Fable filed that papercut separately.

Coordinator ruling F2 (Fable, 2026-09-20), stage markers, and an ownership correction that moved it into M0. The orchestrator's proposed contract asserted a bare 'schema: stub-documents 0'. That cannot satisfy the plan's condition, which is zero stubs among the documents in scope at that milestone: W0.2 pre-declares all 23 documents and M0 delivers five, so a correct M0 build has 18 stubs and --final M0 would have failed on a correct build. Ruling: 40-schema.sh prints one line per pre-declared document, 'schema: <name> implemented' or 'schema: <name> stub'; 45-corpus.sh keeps the proposed corpus spellings; --final carries a per-milestone in-scope list and fails on a stub or an absent marker. The stages are owned by W0.2 (40-schema.sh) and W0.6 (45-corpus.sh), both M0 tasks, so the contract had to exist in their briefs before launch rather than at M2 as the orchestrator first posted. Verified against the plan's owned_files: all 23 documents map to exactly one task, M0's five (snapshot, inventory, capabilities, manifest, error) are all W0.2 and no other W0 task owns anything under schemas/. Recorded in the plan's Interfaces paragraph and in W0.2's and W0.6's delivers at 55f120b; goes into the M0 and M2 review records when those exist.
